text: Meet Ania. She's twenty-seven, earns fifty-eight hundred zloty a month, and she wants a plan that survives surprises. Let's build her monthly money rule. No typing, just blocks.
First, a bit more room. These handles resize the panels, so I'll shrink the task description and the test results, and the workspace gets bigger.
Step one is safety. I drag an if block in, then build its condition: buffer months, less than, two.
Inside it goes save to buffer. So if her emergency fund covers less than two months, every spare zloty goes there first.
Otherwise, I drag in an else.
Dragging isn't the only way. The else is already selected, so I just tap save to pot.
This is her bills pot. The amount is the next bill, minus what's already in the pot, divided by the months left. That way the car insurance never comes as a shock.
Next, debt. If there's anything on her card, she pays it off. A card at twenty percent costs more than almost any investment earns.
If the card is clear but the buffer is still under three months, she keeps building it.

And only then does she invest. Seventy percent of the spare cash goes into a broad fund. I pick the asset from this little menu, and the rest goes into an inflation-linked bond. Spread out, not all on one company.
Here's the code those blocks just wrote. Same plan, as text.
Now the real question. Does it hold up? Run tests: a two-month job loss, a normal two years, and a car repair.
All green. She never borrows on the card, and she still invests over twelve thousand zloty. Submit it, and it faces six hidden events and two hundred possible futures.
